savings.reason: Final savings classification remains unapproved because current-law operative sources are absent. EO14173 section 3 express revocation is immediate; its section 8 authority saving and section 7 scope exclusions do not by themselves establish continuation of these revoked orders. EO11246 optional contractor compliance allowance is a transitional residual, not deferred revocation.

research_rationale: Full frozen-packet recheck: original text is byte-for-byte unchanged while provenance paths and dossier fingerprints changed. Exact original inventory spans were rederived. New actor contexts resolve prior packet omissions; current-law conflicts remain unresolvable because actual legal-text spans are still absent. Part I of EO11246 is expressly superseded by section 7 on 1969-08-08; there is no deferred effective date. Original sections 102,103,105 can use this earlier first end. Sections 101/104 require the earlier EO11375 replacements, whose page verification remains outstanding. The full actor is now held. Its section 2-101 generic redesignation concerns OPM functions; it supplies no express EO11246 numbered amendment. Most importantly it is later than Part I supersession and cannot be the first end of that Part. Default effectiveness is 1979-01-01 under section 2-404. Section 2(a)(i)(G) lists EO11246 among labor laws for disclosures. It is not a revocation of EO11246. Section 10 is immediately effective with solicitation applicability as in FAR rules. Reject the machine whole-order terminate lead. Section 4 borrows EO11246 exemptions/enforcement procedures and permits cancellation of noncomplying contracts; it does not terminate EO11246. Section 9 delays section 4 contract applicability 60 days, not EO11246 cessation. Section 3(d) encourages projects supporting compliance with existing EO11246 obligations. It creates no earlier revocation or supersession of EO11246. General authority and appropriations savings remain relevant but do not establish a present legal predicate. EO14173 section 3(b)(i) hereby revokes EO11246 on 2025-01-21; the full actor context contains no postponed revocation date. The optional 90-day contractor compliance allowance is a transitional residual, not a delay of express revocation. Section 3(b)(ii) immediately ends OFCCP affirmative-action enforcement. EO11375 replaces original sections 101, 104, 202(1)/(2), 203(d). Part I is effective 30 days after 1967-10-13 (candidate 1967-11-12); Part II one year after (candidate 1968-10-13). Actual page verification is required before confirming these dates. EO12086 sections 1-201 through 1-214 change administration/enforcement and numerous original provisions. Section 1-302 defaults conforming amendments to 1978-10-08 but excepts section 1-101 agencies, whose effective dates follow OMB transfer determinations under section 1-301 within 60 days. Signing date 1978-10-05 does not determine those dates. Original section 405 delays activation 30 days and is not a sunset. Original section 403(a) abolishes a committee and transfers records/property; section 403(b) independently preserves prior obligations/directives until revocation or supersession. The 2025 revocation does not demonstrate reversal of completed transfers or extinguishment of accrued obligations.

new_context_findings.finding: Part I of EO11246 is expressly superseded by section 7 on 1969-08-08; there is no deferred effective date. Original sections 102,103,105 can use this earlier first end. Sections 101/104 require the earlier EO11375 replacements, whose page verification remains outstanding.

The full actor is now held. Its section 2-101 generic redesignation concerns OPM functions; it supplies no express EO11246 numbered amendment. Most importantly it is later than Part I supersession and cannot be the first end of that Part. Default effectiveness is 1979-01-01 under section 2-404.
Section 2(a)(i)(G) lists EO11246 among labor laws for disclosures. It is not a revocation of EO11246. Section 10 is immediately effective with solicitation applicability as in FAR rules.

Reject the machine whole-order terminate lead. Section 4 borrows EO11246 exemptions/enforcement procedures and permits cancellation of noncomplying contracts; it does not terminate EO11246. Section 9 delays section 4 contract applicability 60 days, not EO11246 cessation.

Section 3(d) encourages projects supporting compliance with existing EO11246 obligations. It creates no earlier revocation or supersession of EO11246. General authority and appropriations savings remain relevant but do not establish a present legal predicate.

continuing_findings: EO14173 section 3(b)(i) hereby revokes EO11246 on 2025-01-21; the full actor context contains no postponed revocation date. The optional 90-day contractor compliance allowance is a transitional residual, not a delay of express revocation. Section 3(b)(ii) immediately ends OFCCP affirmative-action enforcement.

EO11375 replaces original sections 101, 104, 202(1)/(2), 203(d). Part I is effective 30 days after 1967-10-13 (candidate 1967-11-12); Part II one year after (candidate 1968-10-13). Actual page verification is required before confirming these dates.

EO12086 sections 1-201 through 1-214 change administration/enforcement and numerous original provisions. Section 1-302 defaults conforming amendments to 1978-10-08 but excepts section 1-101 agencies, whose effective dates follow OMB transfer determinations under section 1-301 within 60 days. Signing date 1978-10-05 does not determine those dates.

Original section 405 delays activation 30 days and is not a sunset. Original section 403(a) abolishes a committee and transfers records/property; section 403(b) independently preserves prior obligations/directives until revocation or supersession. The 2025 revocation does not demonstrate reversal of completed transfers or extinguishment of accrued obligations.
